title: Shared principles of human and bacterial antiviral immunity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: no PMCID, not open access in Europe PMC, no supplement, no accessions in text or text-mined, no NCBI links (GEO/SRA/BioProject), no Zenodo/Dryad hits on the DOI. There were no data files to open.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The abstract says it is a Review: a synthesis of published work on cGAS-STING, inflammasomes, argonautes, viperin, CRISPR and anti-phage defence systems. It reports no new measurements.

a1_downloadable.note: A Review article with no deposited dataset, supplement or accessions (checked via Europe PMC, NCBI elink and a Zenodo/Dryad DOI search). The full text is paywalled.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table exists. Any label, such as which defence-system family a protein belongs to, would have to be built from outside databases like DefenseFinder or PADLOC, not taken from this paper.

a3_inputs_present.note: No sequences or features are deposited; the paper only discusses other studies.

a5_enough_rows.note: No rows; the paper has no dataset.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not applicable: there is nothing to load.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists in this paper.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (would only apply to a project built from outside defence-system databases)

honest_claim_h3: None possible: this Review contributes no data of its own to model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequences to predict whether a bacterial protein is an ancestor of a human antiviral immune protein.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need bacterial defence-system and human immune protein sequences from outside databases; this paper supplies none (examples: unknown).
plain_idea.predict: Membership in a shared bacterial-human immune family (for example cGAS-like or viperin-like). The true answers would come from published homology annotations, not from measurements in this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Immunologists and microbiologists hunting for new immune proteins found across kingdoms could use it, but the project would rest entirely on other resources, not on this paper.

ml_idea: None from this paper. A project classifying anti-phage defence proteins would be built on DefenseFinder or PADLOC databases, and would have to be judged as a separate candidate.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no dataset.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether the paper deposits any data: it does not (no PMCID, no supplement, no accessions).

verdict_reason: This is a Nature Review summarising cross-kingdom antiviral immunity. It has no deposited data, supplement or accessions, so it fails A1 (downloadable) and A2 (label is a column) with nothing to model.
